description: Are you a friendly, organised and compassionate person who enjoys helping others and thrives in a busy, team-focused environment? If so, we would love to hear from you. St Peters Health Centre is looking for an enthusiastic Patient Care Advisor (PCA) to join our practice team. As one of the first points of contact for our patients, you will play an important role in making sure every patient feels welcomed, listened to and supported. This is a varied and rewarding role combining excellent customer service with reception and administrative duties. You will help patients access the right care by managing appointment requests, providing clear information, supporting the use of digital services such as SystmConnect and the NHS App, and signposting patients to appropriate NHS and community services. Youll be joining a busy, supportive practice where teamwork and providing an excellent patient experience are at the heart of what we do. We are looking for someone with strong communication and customer service skills who can remain calm under pressure, use their initiative and work positively as part of a wider multidisciplinary team. Previous general practice experience is desirable, but a willingness to learn and develop is equally important. If you are approachable, adaptable and passionate about helping people access the right care, we would be delighted to receive your application. As a Patient Care Advisor, you will be at the heart of the practice, helping patients access the care and support they need while ensuring their experience with us is positive, efficient and compassionate. Your day will be varied and will involve communicating with patients face-to-face, by telephone and through our digital systems. You will listen to patients, understand what they need and help them navigate the most appropriate route for their care. This may include arranging appointments, supporting online requests, providing information or directing patients to other NHS and community services. Alongside patient-facing work, you will carry out a range of administrative tasks to support our clinical team and keep practice services running smoothly. Accuracy, confidentiality and good communication are therefore essential. You will work closely with GPs, nurses, other healthcare professionals and administrative colleagues, supporting one another during busy periods and responding to the changing needs of the practice. This is a busy and responsible role where no two days are quite the same. It would suit someone who enjoys working with people, can prioritise effectively and takes pride in providing excellent service to patients. Patient Care Advisor (PCA) Job Description Responsible to: Patient Care Advisor Team Leader / Patient Care Advisor Manager Accountable to: Patient Care Advisor Manager / Practice Manager Hours: As agreed, with flexibility required to meet service needs. Book, amend and cancel appointments using SystmOne and manage appointment requests in accordance with practice policies and total triage processes. Take accurate messages and ensure timely communication with clinicians and colleagues. Support patients who are unable to complete SystmConnect requests independently and complete requests on their behalf where appropriate. Promote and support the use of the NHS App, SystmConnect and other online services, ensuring sufficient information is obtained to enable appropriate clinical triage. Book, amend and cancel appointments across clinical services, ensuring patients are booked into the most appropriate appointment type. Process new patient and temporary resident registrations, update demographic information, verify identity where required and maintain accurate patient records. Provide administrative support to the clinical team, including raising pathology and diagnostic test requests where authorised, booking interpreters, processing post, scanning and workflowing clinical correspondence and supporting wider practice administrative processes. Maintain accurate and timely information within SystmOne, follow document management procedures and comply with GDPR and Information Governance requirements. Confidentiality must be maintained at all times. Work collaboratively with clinicians and the wider practice team, support colleagues during busy periods and provide cover across reception positions. Participate in team meetings and contribute to service development and improvement. Follow practice policies and procedures, report incidents and patient safety concerns and participate in audits and continuous improvement. description: We are looking to appoint a reliable and motivated receptionist to join our dedicated administration team to support the Community Mental Health Teams at Kings Park Community Hospital. The successful applicant will work as part of a small team, supporting clinical staff and will act as the first point of contact between patients, relatives and medical staff, whilst maintaining confidentiality to ensure the department always runs efficiently. This is a part-time post of 26 hours per week over Monday, Tuesday (1/2 day), Thursday, Friday. The post holder will be required to work flexibly to meet the needs of the service. Applicants must have excellent organizational and communication skills, be able to work under pressure yet remain calm, polite and professional at all times. You will have the ability to deal with varied administrative duties, IT systems and changing priorities. Excellent customer service skills are essential. You will be pleasant and approachable and able to manage your workload effectively. Employment in this post requires an Enhanced Disclosure and Barring Service (DBS) check, which the Trust will cover the cost of. You will provide information to patients, staff, carers, relatives, GPs and the wider Emotional Health and Wellbeing Service relating to appointments, patient care, service pathways and meetings, verbally by telephone, face to face or written in a tactful and courteous manner often requiring non-clinical advice involving careful analysis of delicate situations regarding patient care, requiring knowledge of patient confidentiality. You will liaise with members of the public in their dealings with the team/service, some of whom may prove at times to be distressed, challenging, or aggressive in manner. You will liaise with other members of the service to organise and deliver a safe and efficient office system to support sound patient care, consistent with good clinical governance guidelines, whilst helping the team to achieve targets and complete timely returns of information. All submissions must be truthful and if you do use AI, it should only be used to enhance your application and not create your supporting statement in its entirety. Your supporting statement should be in your own words and must accurately reflect your personal experience and achievements. Where we have concerns that AI has been used to generate content that misrepresents your experience and suitability for the role, we may withdraw your application. As part of our vision to have a skilled, diverse and caring workforce, Dorset HealthCare offers support for people getting into work. We offer an employability service to support individuals with application writing, interview skills and other employment support. description: Are you an organised, proactive administrator looking for an opportunity to develop your career within NHS Legal Services? South London and Maudsley NHS Foundation Trust is looking for an enthusiastic and highly organised Legal Services Administrator to join our busy and supportive Legal Services team. This is a varied role providing administrative and coordination support across a broad range of legal matters, including claims, inquests and Court of Protection matters. You will be an important part of the Legal Services team, helping to ensure that legal matters are managed efficiently, accurately and within required timescales. You will work closely with Legal Services Officer, the Legal Services Manager and colleagues across the Trust. This role would suit someone who enjoys working in a busy environment, takes pride in getting the detail right and is confident dealing with confidential and sometimes sensitive information. You do not need to be a qualified legal professional. We are looking for someone with strong administrative skills, excellent organisation and attention to detail, and an interest in developing their knowledge and experience of NHS Legal Services. You will provide administrative support to the Legal Services team, helping to keep cases, documents and deadlines organised and ensuring that colleagues have the information and support they need. Acting as a first point of contact for routine enquiries to Legal Services and ensuring these are logged, acknowledged and directed appropriately. Maintaining accurate legal case records, databases, trackers and case management systems. Tracking key deadlines, hearings and actions and ensuring records are kept up to date. Supporting the collation of clinical records, policies and other information required for legal matters and disclosure. Assisting with the preparation and collation of legal documents, correspondence, witness statements and evidence bundles. Arranging meetings, case conferences, hearings, calls and witness meetings. Preparing routine correspondence, reports and meeting papers. Liaising with clinical and corporate teams to obtain information and documentation. Communicating professionally and sensitively with staff, patients, families, external solicitors, Coroner's Officers and other agencies. Handling confidential and sensitive information appropriately and in accordance with information governance requirements. Recognising urgent, complex or sensitive matters and escalating them appropriately. Providing general administrative support to the Legal Services team. The postholder will provide comprehensive administrative and coordination support to the Trusts Legal Services function. You will work within agreed processes and procedures, using your initiative to manage your workload and ensure that administrative tasks are completed accurately and within required timescales. You will be expected to recognise when a matter is urgent, complex or sensitive and escalate it to an appropriate member of the Legal Services team. What you will bring Highly organised, with the ability to manage competing priorities and deadlines. Accurate and attentive to detail. Confident using IT systems, including Microsoft Office, Outlook, Word, Excel and databases. Able to maintain accurate records and ensure information is filed and retrievable. A clear and professional communicator, both verbally and in writing. Comfortable working with confidential and sensitive information. Able to work calmly and professionally under pressure. Proactive and able to work independently within defined procedures. A positive team player who is willing to support colleagues and contribute to an efficient and supportive Legal Services function. You will have experience of providing administrative support in a busy office environment, maintaining records or databases, preparing correspondence and documents, arranging meetings and dealing with internal and external stakeholders. Experience of managing competing priorities and deadlines is also important. Experience of working within an NHS, healthcare, legal, governance, claims, complaints, risk or regulatory environment would be advantageous. An awareness of inquests, claims, Court of Protection or Mental Capacity Act processes would also be desirable. You will be educated to A-level standard or have equivalent experience, with GCSE English and Maths or equivalent. A legal secretary, paralegal, CILEX, business administration or healthcare administration qualification would be desirable. Why this role? This is an excellent opportunity for an experienced administrator who wants to develop their skills within a specialist NHS environment. You will gain exposure to a wide variety of legal matters and will work alongside experienced legal professionals while developing your understanding of the processes and governance that underpin NHS Legal Services. If you are organised, approachable and motivated to make a difference, and you are looking for a role where your administrative skills will have a direct impact on the effective delivery of an important Trust function, we would love to hear from you.

description: An exciting opportunity has arisen to join the Maternity Service at Somerset NHS Foundation Trust as a Band 2 Ward Clerk. This is a busy and rewarding role providing administrative, clerical and reception support across maternity inpatient and outpatient areas. As the first point of contact for women, birthing people, families, visitors and staff, you will play a vital role in ensuring an efficient, welcoming and responsive service. You will also provide sensitive and compassionate support when dealing with patients and families who may be anxious or distressed. The successful candidate will have strong administrative and customer service skills, a positive and flexible approach, and a commitment to upholding the Trust values of Kindness, Respect and Teamwork. Flexibility to work across the Maternity Service and assist with service cover, including weekends and extended hours where required, is essential.

description: Tower hill Surgery is seeking a friendly, organised and reliable Receptionist/Care Navigator to join our busy GP surgery team. The successful applicant will be the first point of contact for patients and will play an important role in helping them access the most appropriate service. The role requires excellent communication skills, professionalism and the ability to remain calm and courteous in a busy environment. Main duties Welcoming patients and visitors to the practice. Answering telephone calls and dealing with enquiries appropriately. Booking, cancelling and rearranging appointments in line with practice procedures. Supporting patients to access the most appropriate clinician or NHS service. Using care navigation and signposting processes safely and appropriately. Processing administrative requests, messages and correspondence. Maintaining accurate and confidential patient records. Liaising with GPs, nurses, administrative colleagues and other members of the multidisciplinary team. Supporting online, telephone and face-to-face access routes. Identifying urgent requests and escalating them to the appropriate clinician in accordance with practice protocols. Treating patients, carers and colleagues with respect and courtesy. Working in accordance with information governance, confidentiality, safeguarding and health and safety requirements. The Medical Receptionist/Care Navigator plays a crucial role in supporting patients by guiding them through the healthcare system, ensuring they receive the appropriate care and services. This position involves working closely with patients, GPs, and other healthcare professionals to coordinate care and improve patient outcomes. To be responsible for undertaking a wide range of reception duties and the provision of general support to the multidisciplinary team. Duties can include, but are not limited to, greeting and directing patients, effective use of the appointment system, booking appointments, the processing of information and assisting patients as required. To act as the central point of contact for patients, be responsible for the distribution of information, messages and enquires for the clinical team and external agencies such as secondary care and community service providers. Patient Support: Act as the first point of contact for patients, providing information and assistance with navigating healthcare services. Appointment Coordination: Schedule and manage patient appointments, ensuring they are booked with the appropriate healthcare professional. Care Coordination: Work with GPs and other healthcare providers to coordinate patient care, including referrals to specialists and community services. Information Provision: Provide patients with information about available services, health resources, and self-care management. Communication: Maintain clear and effective communication with patients, healthcare providers, and other stakeholders. Record Keeping: Accurately update and maintain patient records and appointment schedules. Problem Solving: Address patient queries and concerns, escalating issues to the appropriate healthcare professional when necessary. Generic Responsibilities All staff at this organisation have a duty to conform to the following : Equality, Diversity and Inclusion A good attitude and positive action towards equality, diversity and inclusion creates an environment where all individuals can achieve their full potential. All personnel have a duty to take reasonable care of health and safety at work for themselves, their team and others and to co-operate with employers to ensure compliance with health and safety requirements. The security of the organisation is the responsibility of all personnel. The post holder must ensure they always remain vigilant and report any suspicious activity immediately to their line manager. Confidentiality The organisation is committed to maintaining an outstanding confidential service. Patients entrust and permit us to collect and retain sensitive information relating to their health and other matters pertaining to their care. It is essential that, if the legal requirements are to be met and the trust of our patients is to be retained, all staff must protect patient information and provide a confidential service. Quality and Continuous Improvement To preserve and improve the quality of this organisations outputs, all personnel are required to think not only of what they do but how they achieve it. By continually examining our processes, we will be able to develop and improve the overall effectiveness of the way we work. The responsibility for this rests with everyone working within the organisation to look for opportunities to improve quality and share good practice and to discuss, highlight and work with the team to create opportunities to improve patient care. Learning and Development The effective use of training and development is fundamental in ensuring that all staff are equipped with the appropriate skills, knowledge, attitude and competencies to perform their role. All staff will be required to partake in, and complete, mandatory training as directed. It is an expectation for this post holder to assess their own learning needs and undertake learning as appropriate. Induction We will provide a full induction programme and management will support you throughout this process. Collaborative working All staff are to recognise the significance of collaborative working and understand their own role and scope and identify how this may develop over time. Staff are to prioritise their own workload and ensure effective time-management strategies are embedded within the culture of the team. Teamwork is essential in multidisciplinary environments and the post holder is to work as an effective and responsible team member, supporting others and exploring the mechanisms to develop new ways of working and work effectively with others to clearly define values, direction and policies impacting upon care delivery. Effective communication is essential and all staff must ensure they communicate in a manner which enables the sharing of information in an appropriate manner. title: Patient Administrator
description: This is a small, friendly and busy GP Practice where no two days are the same. We are looking for a Patient Administrator to join our supportive team and play an important role in helping our patients access the right care at the right time. The role is fast-paced, varied and sometimes challenging, so you will need to be organised, calm under pressure and able to manage several tasks at once. You will be dealing with patients face-to-face and over the telephone, supporting appointments and enquiries, processing administrative work and working closely with our clinical and administrative teams. It can be demanding, but it is also extremely rewarding. Every day you will have the opportunity to make a genuine difference to someone's experience of the NHS whether that is helping a patient navigate the practice, resolving a problem, or simply providing a friendly and reassuring point of contact. We value teamwork, kindness, reliability and a willingness to learn. In return, you will join a close-knit team where your contribution matters and where every member of staff plays an important part in delivering a high-quality service to our patients. If you enjoy working with people, thrive in a busy environment and want a role where no two days are the same, we would love to hear from you. Previous GP or NHS experience is desirable, but full training will be provided. We will only contact candidates who are shortlisted for interview. If invited you will be required to complete a typing test. We are seeking a part-time, permanent Patient Administrator to join our amazing team. Hours: 16.5 hours over 3 days Monday: 1:00pm - 6:00pm Wednesday: 1:00pm - 6:45pm Friday: 1:00pm - 6:45pm Brief Description of Duties As a Patient Administrator, you will be one of the first points of contact for our patients and will play an important role in helping them access the right service at the right time. Your duties will include: Welcoming and assisting patients at reception in a friendly and professional manner. Answering telephone calls and responding to patient enquiries. Supporting patients with appointments and directing them to the most appropriate service or member of the team. Responding to emails and online enquiries, including our online triage system. Processing repeat prescription requests and dealing with prescription-related administrative queries. Undertaking DOCMAN administration, including scanning, coding and filing incoming. Filing and maintaining patient records and ensuring information is processed accurately and promptly. Completing general administrative tasks to support the smooth running of the practice. Liaising with clinical and non-clinical teams. Handling confidential and sensitive information in accordance with practice policies and NHS requirements. Current patients of the Surgery: If you are offered this position, you would need to register with another GP practice before commencing employment with us. RESPONSIBILITIES To provide a friendly, professional and helpful first point of contact for patients and visitors to the Surgery. To deal with patients by telephone, face-to-face, email and through the Practice's online triage system. To assist patients with appointments, queries and requests and direct them to the appropriate service, clinician or member of the Practice team. To undertake a range of reception and administrative duties to support the smooth and effective running of the Practice. To process patient information and administrative work accurately and in accordance with Practice protocols. To maintain patient confidentiality and comply with information governance and data protection requirements. To work collaboratively with both clinical and administrative colleagues. To remain calm, professional, helpful and courteous when dealing with patients, including during challenging or difficult interactions. TASKS TELEPHONE To log in to the Practice telephony system and respond to telephone calls as quickly and effectively as possible. To deal with, transfer or escalate calls as appropriate, following Practice protocols. To accept, record and transmit information accurately using EMIS, online triage system, generic email and other Practice computer systems. To assist patients with queries, requests and access to appropriate services. To provide a professional, calm and courteous service, including when dealing with challenging or difficult telephone interactions. To maintain confidentiality when discussing patient information over the telephone. To log out of the telephony system at the end of each working session. RECEPTION To receive patients and visitors arriving at the Practice in a welcoming, friendly and professional manner. To assist with patient queries and requests or pass messages to the appropriate person. To confidently navigate patient records using EMIS, Docman and other Practice systems in order to assist with patient queries. To make appointments for patients with the appropriate Practice service using EMIS, where required. To assist patients with the Practice's online triage system, including explaining how to access and use the service and directing patients to the appropriate route where required. To handle queries and requests for information or services and ensure that they are dealt with appropriately or transferred to a GP, healthcare professional, member of staff or outside agency in accordance with Practice protocols. To respond appropriately to patient queries received through generic email and other electronic communication channels, ensuring enquiries are dealt with or passed to the appropriate person. To maintain a professional and courteous approach at all times, including when dealing with challenging situations. ADMINISTRATION To undertake general administrative duties required for the smooth running of the Practice. To process repeat prescription requests and deal with prescription-related administrative queries in accordance with Practice protocols. To undertake DOCMAN administration, including receiving, scanning, attaching, coding and filing correspondence accurately into the correct patient's medical record and routing correspondence to the appropriate clinician or team. To process incoming hospital letters, clinic correspondence and other clinical documentation, ensuring that information is accurately recorded and reaches the appropriate clinician or member of the Practice team. To undertake general filing and maintain accurate and appropriately organised patient records. To respond to patient emails and electronic enquiries appropriately and within Practice protocols. To undertake administrative work relating to QOF call and recall lists when required. To assist with deductions from the Practice patient list/records in accordance with Practice procedures and guidance. To assist with administrative backlogs and other Practice administrative work as required. To accurately enter, update and maintain patient information using EMIS, Docman, online triage system and other Practice systems. To ensure that all patient information is handled securely and confidentially and in accordance with Practice policies, information governance requirements and data protection legislation. GENERAL To assist as required during periods of staff holiday, sickness, increased workload or other operational requirements. To work collaboratively with clinical and administrative colleagues, supporting one another and contributing positively to the wider Practice team. To undertake any other reasonable duties appropriate to the role as requested by the Practice Manager or Partners. To attend and complete Practice training and develop the knowledge and skills required for the role. To follow all Practice policies, procedures and protocols and raise any concerns with the Practice Manager. To maintain a professional, respectful, helpful and courteous approach towards patients, colleagues and other healthcare professionals. To remain calm and professional when dealing with challenging situations and seek assistance from an appropriate colleague where necessary. To contribute to the Practice's commitment to providing safe, compassionate and high-quality care to patients. To maintain confidentiality at all times and not disclose patient or Practice information except in accordance with Practice procedures and relevant legislation.

You will need to manage your workload, follow practice and national guidance, and know when to seek advice from a GP, supervisor or manager. (7.5 hour shift per day) BENEFITS: Pension - 5% employer contribution based on qualified earnings. VIVUP - Supermarket & High Street Discounts & Employee Assistant Programme. Blue Light Card - Supermarket & High Street Discounts. Employee referral scheme. 28 days annual leave including Bank Holidays (pro-rata). Main duties of the job The post holder will be responsible for promoting, delivering, and facilitating various programmes directed by management as part of the School-Aged Immunisation Service assisting nurses in the schools or office. KEY RESPONSIBILITIES: Assist in the planning, delivery and evaluation of health promotion/education and public health school age immunisation programmes. Attend community-based vaccination sessions in both schools and local based settings. Work with the nursing team to ensure productive and safe sessions. Promote and facilitate collaborative working between the team, schools and other educational institutions and families, in the delivery of the immunisation programmes. Focus on ensuring all consent forms have been returned, guaranteeing new ideas go towards achieving local area targets. Ensure the process for storing, transporting, collecting and delivering vaccinations to site are adhered to. Assist in identifying home schooled children and those in Pupil Referral Units. Maintain databases to ensure records are kept up to date and that documents are prepared for school visits. Ensure online consent systems have been triaged and completed ahead of a vaccination session. Adhere to the Standard Operating Procedure for School Immunisation (SOPs). First point of contact for all administrative tasks. Have clear communication via face to face, by phone and email with children, parents and school staff. Responsible for maintaining the cold chain, ordering, and arranging transport of vaccinations to site. Actively and constructively contribute to team meetings. Undertake other duties commensurate with the level of this position. Comply with Company policies & procedures.

employer: South London and Maudsley NHS Foundation Trust
description: This position is five day a week (Mon to Fri) on site with no remote working. The trust does not offer visa sponsorship for this post. Tyson West 1 is part of Bethlem Royal Hospital. We offer services for men, aged 18-65, who have acute mental illness and require 24 hour hospital care. Acute illnesses start quickly and have distressing symptoms.We provide care for people who live in the London Borough of Croydon.We offer psychiatric assessment, care and treatment in hospital, which helps to reduce the risk to self and others.Our service brings together teams of health and social care professionals, including nurses, psychologists, OTs, social workers and psychiatrists. This position is five day a week on site with no remote working. We are looking for a highly organised, efficient, flexible and proactive person with excellent communication skills to work in the busy post, and who can balance work demands along with the changing needs of the service. The role requires the post holder to communicate with patients, ward staff and visitors, and to develop collaborative working relationships with colleagues and external agencies. The post holder must have an excellent telephone manner, good IT skills with experience using Microsoft Office packages (Work, Excel and Outlook) . Other tasks include, but not limited to, ordering of stationery, processing of post, scanning, monitoring and ordering ward stock and other tasks (see job description). You must be able to prioritise your workload, be effective at implementing good working practices as well as having a flexible and proactive approach to work in order to cover colleagues when required. Be responsible for the provision of a high-quality reception and administrative service for a busy acute ward. Reception:To provide an effective and efficient reception and administrative services, which will include dealing with telephone enquiries, taking accurate messages and pass them promptly to the appropriate member of the team. Dealing with the public, face-to-face, in a courteous andkind manner and identifying and informing as appropriate the responsible professional worker. To monitor supplies of patient information such as welcome packs.Administration:To assist in providing a comprehensive administrative service to the multi-disciplinary teams, which include but not limited to data inputting patient information, scanning documents and uploading to patient database. Maintaining efficient and effective administration systems to support the needs of the service, working with other members of the admin team as appropriate to achieve this. To assist in providing accurate and efficient data entry into Trust information systems and to assist in the collection of statistical information for the Trust. To assist in the booking of interpreters, taxis etc. Service Requirements:To undertake any other duties as required for the service by the Business Manager or Team Leaders.To deliver a high standard of customer care, representative or the service and the overall Trust objectives and commitments. Exercise diplomacy and professionalism, confidentially and equality standards in accordance with all Trust policies. Staff DevelopmentTo attend regular supervision and annual appraisal meetings. To participate in any training and developmental needs as required by the Business Manager.To complete all identified mandatory training and ensure this is kept up-to-date.
